sections.offseason:
**Buffalo:** fired Sean McDermott in January, promoted OC Joe Brady to head coach, hired Pete Carmichael as OC (keeps the downfield-passing identity) and Jim Leonhard (ex-Broncos) as DC, who is converting a defense that ranked 30th vs. the run in 2025 (5.14 YPC) from a 4-2-5 into a multiple, attacking 3-4.
- **Detroit:** kept DC Kelvin Sheppard, but he's expanding nickel usage and blending 4-3/3-4 fronts after the defense was exploitable on early downs in 2025.
- **Detroit roster hit:** lost RB David Montgomery to Houston in free agency; his replacement Isiah Pacheco just had back surgery and is out for a significant stretch, and CB Terrion Arnold was released — leaving Jahmyr Gibbs a true workhorse and the secondary thin.
- **Week 1 changed the picture:** Detroit's safety-less secondary (Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph both start the year on PUP) got carved up after halftime by New Orleans (31-30 OT loss allowed); Buffalo's new Leonhard defense gave up 124 rush yards (3.9 YPC) and a big day to ex-Lion Montgomery in a 36-31 shootout win over Houston.
sections.matchup:
**DET offense vs. BUF defense:** Jahmyr Gibbs (29 att/156 yds/2 TD, 5 catches Week 1) is the focal point and profiles as a plus matchup vs. a Bills front still installing Leonhard's 3-4 that just allowed 124 rush yards/3.9 YPC. Amon-Ra St. Brown is Detroit's high-volume red-zone/possession piece (10-of-14, 2 TD) while Jameson Williams remains boom-or-bust downfield (4-of-9, 45 yds) and Sam LaPorta is a steady 6-8 target TE who could find seams if Buffalo's retooled LB corps struggles in coverage the way Detroit's did against Kincaid.
- **BUF offense vs. DET defense:** Josh Allen (20-of-29, 334 yds, 2 pass TD, 2 rush TD Week 1) faces a Lions secondary without both starting safeties and now without Arnold at corner; expect heavy volume again for Dalton Kincaid (130 yds Week 1, most by a Bills TE since 1967) and DJ Moore (100 yds, TD). Detroit's pass rush (5 sacks on Tyler Shough, led by a healthy Aidan Hutchinson) is the counterpunch against a Bills O-line adjusting to a new staff.

sections.offseason:
**Atlanta** hired HC Kevin Stefanski (ex-Browns) this offseason, with Matt Ryan elevated to president of football ops and Ian Cunningham as GM — a full front-office reset. The Falcons enter Week 2 in a QB crisis: Tua Tagovailoa (oblique) and Michael Penix Jr. (recovering from a partially torn ACL) are both OUT, leaving veteran journeyman Cooper Rush as the starter after he went 12/22 for 143 yards, 1 TD, 2 INT in a 20-13 Week 1 loss to Pittsburgh. Defensively ATL is thin up front — James Pearce opened suspended and Jalon Walker is out for the season (ACL) — with reports pointing to only 5 new starters up front and a run defense that ranked 23rd/27th in YPC/explosive-run-rate allowed last year.
- **Carolina** retained DC Ejiro Evero and invested heavily on defense (Jaelan Phillips, Devin Lloyd, plus ex-Rams Christian Rozeboom, Bobby Brown III, A'Shawn Robinson) to push for a top-10 unit — but Week 1 was a disaster, allowing 59 points/552 yards in a shootout loss to Chicago (3 CAR turnovers didn't help). Bryce Young authored his best opener yet (23/37, 361 yds, 3 TD, 1 INT, rush TD) behind Dave Canales's power-run-first, play-action scheme.
sections.matchup:
**CAR offense vs ATL defense:** Atlanta's run D was a bottom-third unit in 2025 (4.5 YPC, 27th in explosive-run rate) and now starts several new front-seven pieces — a soft matchup for Chuba Hubbard/Jonathon Brooks behind Canales's power scheme. Through the air, ATL allowed 7.1 YPA (20th) and got torched underneath in Week 1; Tetairoa McMillan (5-8-75 Wk1) profiles as a target hog against a secondary anchored by A.J. Terrell and Jessie Bates but without much depth behind them.
- **ATL offense vs CAR defense:** Carolina's D just allowed 552 yards/59 points to Chicago, but Cooper Rush's limited arm and 2 INT last week cap the ceiling. Bijan Robinson is the engine (21 carries/83 yds + 8-10-90-1 receiving in Wk1) and his red-zone/goal-line share should climb now that Tyler Allgeier is gone; Drake London (2-4-29) and Kyle Pitts (0-1) were quiet in Wk1 and face a CAR front that added real juice (Phillips, Lloyd) even after the Wk1 letdown.
sections.injuries:
**CAR:** WR Jalen Coker (left ankle, boot) is Questionable but self-reported optimism about playing; LB Patrick Jones II is Out (back); the defense otherwise looks healthy with Derrick Brown, Jaelan Phillips and Akayleb Evans all clearing the injury list.
- **ATL:** QBs Tua Tagovailoa and Michael Penix Jr. are both Out, confirming Cooper Rush starts. DT Da'Shawn Hand (torn quad) is Out for the season. G Chris Lindstrom (foot/concussion) and DL Brandon Dorlus (oblique), DL Zach Harrison (knee), and CB Mike Hughes (neck) are Questionable game-time decisions; G Matthew Bergeron (ankle) and DE Leonard Floyd (hamstring) are Out for a second straight week — a genuinely banged-up O-line in front of a third-string QB.

sections.offseason:
- **CHI**: Year 2 under HC **Ben Johnson** (hired from Detroit's OC chair); he said the goal was to chase the NFL's single-season scoring record, and Chicago backed it up with 59 points, 552 total yards (291 rush/261 pass) and 6 rushing TDs in a Week 1 rout of Carolina, splitting work between **D'Andre Swift** (19 touches, 134 yds, 3 TD) and **Kyle Monangai** (12 touches, 124 yds, 1 TD).
- Bears defense (DC **Dennis Allen**) allowed 37 points/leaky red-zone snaps in Week 1 and is now without DT Shemar Turner, CB Kyler Gordon (PUP, calf) and CB Dallis Flowers (IR); RT Ozzy Trapilo (knee) and S Xavier Woods are out again for Week 2.
- **MIN**: HC **Kevin O'Connell** won 39-22 at Green Bay, but new starter **Kyler Murray** left in the first quarter with a concussion; veteran **Carson Wentz** relieved him and threw for 133 yds and 3 TDs.
- DC **Brian Flores** unveiled an ultra-aggressive 6-1/double-mug scheme, blitzing roughly 82% of snaps to mask a young secondary; offseason DL/secondary additions give him more bodies to rotate.
- Both clubs are 1-0, but Minnesota now carries QB uncertainty (Murray day-to-day) while Chicago is banged up on the O-line and in the back end.
sections.matchup:
- **CHI offense vs MIN defense**: Ben Johnson's zone-run/play-action attack piled up 291 rush yards Wk1; Flores' pressure-heavy, box-loading scheme is built to clog those same run lanes but its all-out blitz rate also invites explosive shots downfield to Rome Odunze/Luther Burden III/Kalif Raymond (20 combined targets, 199 yds Wk1). Chicago's banged-up interior (Trapilo out at RT) is a soft spot for Minnesota's edge duo of Jonathan Greenard and Dallas Turner.
- **MIN offense vs CHI defense**: Whoever starts at QB leans on Justin Jefferson (8-92-2, ~28-32% target share) and TE T.J. Hockenson (4-36-1) underneath and in the red zone. Chicago's secondary is thin (Gordon out, Woods out, Flowers on IR) but top corner Jaylon Johnson is healthy and figures to travel with Jefferson, leaving backups to handle Hockenson/Jauan Jennings inside.
- Red zone: Chicago scored 6 rushing TDs Wk1 (heavy goal-to-go run plan for Swift/Williams); Minnesota mixed ground (Aaron Jones) and air (Jefferson x2, Hockenson) scores, a more balanced red-zone profile.

- **CHI**: OT Ozzy Trapilo (knee), S Xavier Woods (groin), QB Tyson Bagent, CB Kyler Gordon (calf, on PUP) and DT Shemar Turner all Out; CB Dallis Flowers on IR. Starters Jaylon Johnson (arm), Austin Booker (groin), Elijah Hicks (shin) and Keyshaun Elliott are off the injury report.

Secondary overhauled — released L'Jarius Sneed, traded Roger McCreary, signed **Cor'Dale Flott** and **Alontae Taylor**. WR room reloaded with rookies Carnell Tate/Elic Ayomanor plus vets Calvin Ridley/Wan'Dale Robinson; center Andre James landed on IR, thinning an already shaky line. Traded for DK Metcalf and signed Michael Pittman Jr. to remake the WR room around Rodgers. Week 1: beat Atlanta 20-13 on a takeaway-driven defensive effort (5 turnovers, incl. a T.J. Watt pick-six plus 2.0 sacks) while the offense scored only one touchdown (Rodgers 24/40, 221 yds, 1 TD, 0 INT) — an efficiency win, not an explosive one.
- **NE:** Year 2 of the Mike Vrabel/Josh McDaniels (3rd stint as NE OC) regime, riding Drake Maye's breakout 2025 season. Lost WR1 A.J. Brown to IR (high-ankle sprain, ~6 weeks) right before kickoff, thinning the room to Hollins/Douglas/Doubs/Chism III. Week 1: 13-10 loss to Seattle — Maye threw 3 INTs (23/33, 178 yds, 1 TD) despite 47 rush yards; the defense (Gonzalez, Byard, Spillane) held Seattle to 13 points and posted a top-10 EPA/play mark allowed.
sections.matchup:
- **PIT offense vs. NE defense:** New England's defense was stout in the opener (top-8 EPA/play allowed) behind All-Pro CB Christian Gonzalez, new S Kevin Byard, and DT DaQuan Jones (just signed) bolstering the interior run defense. Metcalf drew a game-high 10 targets but caught only 4 for 40 yds — Gonzalez should travel with him, pushing volume to Freiermuth (5-of-5, 46 yds, TD) and the backfield (Warren 5-of-6 targets, 27 yds). Pittsburgh's run game was inefficient (Warren 10-46, Dowdle 8-15) behind a line missing OT Jack Driscoll (IR).
- **NE offense vs. PIT defense:** Pittsburgh allowed a top-5 EPA/play mark in Week 1 and forced five takeaways; T.J. Watt (2.0 sacks) and Alex Highsmith give the Steelers a legitimate pass-rush duo versus an O-line that allowed 47 sacks last season (Maye was addressed this offseason via 1st-round OT Caleb Lomu). With A.J. Brown out, Maye leans on Stevenson as a receiving/goal-line option (5-of-6 targets, 44 yds Wk1) and Hunter Henry/Eli Raridon in the red zone (Raridon's lone target was a 2-yd TD). Expect Pittsburgh to key on Stevenson and make Hollins/Douglas beat man coverage from Ramsey/Samuel Jr.

**New York Jets**
- HC Aaron Glenn (3-14 in Year 1) overhauled 12 of 22 assistants; fired OC Tanner Engstrand and DC Steve Wilks
- Hired veteran Frank Reich as OC/play-caller; Glenn himself is calling the defense again with new coordinator Brian Duker assisting
- Let Aaron Rodgers and Davante Adams walk; signed Geno Smith at QB
- Reloaded defense with Minkah Fitzpatrick, Demario Davis and David Onyemata after finishing 2025 30th in passing points allowed

sections.offseason:
**Browns:** New HC **Todd Monken** (ex-Ravens OC) replaces Kevin Stefanski. Cleveland traded 2x DPOY **Myles Garrett to the Rams** for DE **Jared Verse** plus draft capital, and restructured **Deshaun Watson's** guaranteed deal to keep him as 2026 starter over Shedeur Sanders. The O-line was overhauled (voided deals for Bitonio/Teller/Pocic/Conklin; rookie **Spencer Fano** at LT, **Tytus Howard** RT, **Elgton Jenkins** at center). Week 1 was a disaster: 34-10 loss at Jacksonville, Watson 16/22-205-1TD-1INT, and the defense lost **Grant Delpit, Maurice Hurst, and Ogbo Okoronkwo to season-ending injuries** while allowing a 150.6 rating to Trevor Lawrence.
- **Buccaneers:** New OC **Zac Robinson** (ex-Falcons) replaces Josh Grizzard; new ST coordinator **Danny Smith**. Pass rush was a stated offseason priority (added Rueben Bain Jr., David Walker, retained Yaya Diaby/Al-Quadin Muhammad) but Week 1 pressure was minimal (Calijah Kancey led with just 4 pressures; Bain Jr. had zero on 24 rushes). TB lost a 33-27 shootout to Cincinnati, undone by **4 turnovers/3 first-half fumbles**, not a broken defense — Baker Mayfield actually went 23/28-216 with a rushing TD.
sections.matchup: **TB offense vs CLE defense:** Cleveland's secondary is now thin after losing Delpit/Hurst/Okoronkwo in Week 1, and the front seven (anchored by newly acquired Jared Verse) has yet to show it can replace Garrett's pressure — Jacksonville torched them for 355 total yards. That sets up well for **Egbuka (5/6-63) and Godwin (4/4-40)** on the perimeter and Bucky Irving as a checkdown/receiving weapon (7/7-48 targets Week 1). **CLE offense vs TB defense:** TB ranked top-5 vs the run (99.1 YPG) under Todd Bowles but was dead-last (32nd) in red-zone TD rate allowed last year (69.8%), a real inefficiency Cleveland's banged-up offense could exploit near the goal line even if it can't sustain drives. Backfield is now a three-man committee (J.K. Dobbins/RJ Harvey/rookie Jonah Coleman), with Harvey pushed toward a third-down/receiving role. Defense returns the league's top pass rush (68 sacks in 2025 - Nik Bonitto, Zach Allen, Pat Surtain II, Talanoa Hufanga), but LB Jonathon Cooper is out indefinitely amid a domestic-violence case and the OL is already thin.
- **Week 1 shift:** JAX throttled CLE 34-10 - Lawrence 18/23-245-4TD-0INT (150.6 rating), scoring on 6 of 7 possessions; D had 5 sacks and 2 takeaways. DEN was embarrassed 31-10 by KC on MNF - Nix opened sacked, threw a pick two plays later, finished 17/28-131-1TD-1INT with 3 fumbles (1 lost); DEN allowed 221 rush yards (173 to Kenneth Walker) and drew 7 penalties for 52 yards.

sections.offseason:
**Giants:** Fired Brian Daboll in Nov. 2025 and hired John Harbaugh (ex-Ravens, 18 years) as HC in January, pairing him with DC Dennard Wilson and OC Matt Nagy. Traded DT Dexter Lawrence to Cincinnati for the No. 10 pick; released longtime WR Darius Slayton. Signed TE Isaiah Likely, LB Tremaine Edmunds and CB Greg Newsome II. Jaxson Dart is the unquestioned starter and was excellent in the opener (23/29, 230 yds, 3 TD, plus 54 rush yds) in a 28-20 win over Dallas that doubled as Harbaugh's debut.
- **Rams:** Sean McVay enters Year 10 with new OC Nathan Scheelhaase and new DC Chris Shula. Made two blockbuster trades — sent Jared Verse to Cleveland for reigning DPOY Myles Garrett, and shipped picks to Kansas City for CB Trent McDuffie — and Aaron Donald un-retired in August. Week 1 was a disaster in Melbourne: 27-7 loss to SF, Stafford 15/25-155-1 INT, and only two total QB hits allowed on defense. Garrett (0 pressures, 40 snaps) had a knee scope Monday and is now on IR through at least Week 6.
sections.matchup: **NYG offense vs LAR defense:** The Rams' pass rush was toothless in Week 1 and now loses Garrett for the year with Donald's Week 2 status "TBD" per McVay — a green light for a Giants O-line that allowed no sacks last week. Isaiah Likely (8 tgt, 2 TD) profiles as a matchup problem for a Rams LB group nursing Landman (shoulder/thumb) and Speights (hip); Cam Skattebo is the clear goal-line back (18 carries, TD, zero targets) while Devin Singletary siphons receiving-down work. Malik Nabers, back from ACL surgery, still drew 9 targets. **LAR offense vs NYG defense:** Giants' D ranked 5th in yards and 5th vs the run in Week 1 and returns an elite front (Brian Burns, Abdul Carter, Kayvon Thibodeaux, Tremaine Edmunds) that should pressure a Stafford who was rattled in Australia. Kyren Williams is the bell-cow and Puka Nacua/Davante Adams give Stafford two true red-zone targets, but LAR's TE room is muddled with no clear separator.
sections.injuries: **LAR:** Myles Garrett (knee) — OUT/IR, targeting Week 6. Aaron Donald (rest/undisclosed) — status TBD, did not travel to Melbourne. Nate Landman (shoulder/thumb) — Questionable, expected to play. Omar Speights (hip pointer) — Questionable, trending toward playing. Kam Curl (ankle) — Questionable. **NYG:** No players carry a Week 2 game-status designation as of Monday; Colton Hood, Francis Mauigoa, Greg Newsome II, John Michael Schmitz, Dru Phillips and Paulson Adebo all cleared last week's report and played. Roy Robertson-Harris (DT) remains on IR.
